children: The Swiss firm's market value fell over $30 bln after a drug acquired in a recent takeover disappointed, prompting calls for a board shake-up. But expiring patents in coming years will force CEO Vas Narasimhan to do deals. That may be harder if he is distracted by investor anger.
Full view will be published shortly.

A major shareholder in Novartis on September 10 called for a shake-up of the Swiss drugmaker's board to improve corporate governance after its shares suffered a record fall following back-to-back trial setbacks.

David Samra, managing director at top 20 investor Artisan Partners and founding partner of International Value Group, said the board needed to strengthen its oversight of acquisitions, calling for action from board chairman Giovanni Caforio.

On September 8, a muscle-wasting disorder drug acquired through Novartis' $12 billion takeover of U.S. firm Avidity failed a late-stage study, sending the company's shares tumbling more than 10% and wiping over $30 billion off its market value.
Novartis' stock, which had been up some 20% year-to-date before this week's slide, had already fallen a day earlier after results from heart drug pelacarsen disappointed investors.
